newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bank of Spain cuts rate, more reductions seen.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Spain cuts rate, more reductions seen.

text.p: The Bank of Spain caught markets off-guard Thursday with an unexpectedly swift quarter-point reduction in its official interest rate.

The central bank cut its key money market rate to 6 percent, a historic low, just one month after it slashed the interest rate by half a point. The Bank of Spain has steered the rate down from 9 percent at the start of 1996.
Economists said the latest cut was just the beginning of declines in the interest rate this year.

Stocks and bonds rose on the news. The 10-year bond outpaced its sturdier German counterpart and the yield drove to parity with the U.S. benchmark 30-year Treasury bond for the first time ever -- a sign the market sees no extra risk in Spanish over U.S. issues.
Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato, speaking at a seminar, attributed the reduction to a moderation in inflation but said more work needed to be done to contain prices.
Economists agreed, but added that the peseta's strength may also have played a key role.

After months of straining at the bit, the peseta broke free last Friday and stormed through the barrier of 84 to the German mark after the Bank of Spain released its frim grip and refrained from intervening.
